description: Blackened shell webbed with live lava, cut out of a Magmane. A weapon takes its fire and leaves things burning.
lore: The standing argument about [[monsters/obsidian_lion|the lion]] is whether any of the heat is its own. It is Made, so nothing in it ever lived anywhere else: remembering that gathered at a volcano's throat, thickened, and stood up. And everything on that ground is hot, the boulders included. Stand close and you have stood near a hot animal on hot rock, with nothing in it you can separate.

The stone settles that. A blackened shell webbed with live lava, brightest where the webs meet; two hundred and eighty-five gold; and still exactly that hot at the bottom of a pack four hundred miles west, in a wet country, in winter, with the mountain nowhere in it. The heat came away when the stone did.

Off an edge it goes in and stays in: what you struck is still burning while you decide what to do next. That follows from the animal. The fire is shut under the glass and opens only once it has decided about you, and it does not decide twice.

[[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] charges for the iron rather than the setting — a housing that touches a web has to be forged around the stone in place, with the stone in the fire throughout and indifferent to it. She has done four. Over each one she says the same sentence to whoever is paying, in the flat voice she keeps for people who want a thing and would rather not know about it: this will still be doing that when you have stopped.
gm_notes: Osric is deliberately absent — his record owns the great heat he cannot use, and repeating him would hand a reader the same page twice. The other four burnt-country stones own handling, tins of sand, held heat and the lit centre, so this one takes provenance (the heat is the animal's, not the mountain's) and the setting problem. Sigrun's closing sentence is hers, not a trade saying.
